description:
**ROADMAP Phase 1, the gate itself. CI has been red on every run in its life.** Re-observed 2026-09-11 on run `34556064209` (main, head `5ac68e3`): `ios` FAILURE; `android`, `react-native`, `conformance-fixture`, `verify-policy` SUCCESS. The `ios` job dies in its FIRST step (`swift build --package-path ios -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`, `emit-module command failed`) on exactly two errors:

- `ios/Sources/Amphora/Governor/NetworkGovernor.swift:23:26: error: reference to captured var 'self' in concurrently-executing code`
- `ios/Sources/Amphora/Transport/TUSKitTransport.swift:27:17: error: stored property 'session' of 'Sendable'-conforming struct 'TUSKitTransport' has non-sendable type 'BackgroundSessionManager'`

so `swift run AmphoraPathTests` and the Swift drift control have never once executed in CI.

**Why the local gate cannot see them — measured while authoring, 2026-09-11.** The local toolchain is Swift 6.3.3 (macOS 26 SDK); CI is `macos-14-arm64` (image 20260831.0302) with its default Xcode. A CLEAN local `swift build --package-path ios -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` exits 0. Adding `-Xswiftc -strict-concurrency=complete` locally surfaces the same defect from the other side: `BackgroundSessionManager.swift:29:17: error: stored property 'systemCompletionHandler' of 'Sendable'-conforming class 'BackgroundSessionManager' is mutable` (plus an unrelated `SQLiteUploadStore.swift:42:28` deinit finding). The likely reading — an inference, not verified — is that the newer SDK makes the class implicitly `Sendable` through `URLSessionDelegate`, so the struct error vanishes locally and reappears as a mutability error under complete checking, while on CI's older SDK the class is not `Sendable` at all. Either way there is one root: `BackgroundSessionManager` has mutable state (`systemCompletionHandler`, the `lazy var session`) and no concurrency model. ROADMAP §4 records that model as owned by nobody and says Phase 1 forces the answer. This tasklist is the answer.

**Must NOT depend on ADR-0002.** Whether iOS 17 becomes the minimum — which would delete `TUSKitTransport` — is an open operator decision. The fix holds at the current `platforms: [.iOS(.v15), .macOS(.v14)]` with `TUSKitTransport` in place; if ADR-0002 later deletes it, nothing here should need undoing.

**The android job is green today, and that proves nothing about the kapt failure.** `:android:kaptReleaseKotlin` failed with `java.lang.IllegalStateException: Empty schema file` at `androidx.room.migration.bundle.SchemaBundle$Companion.deserialize(SchemaBundle.kt:69)` <- `androidx.room.vo.Database.exportSchema(Database.kt:110)` on run `33044503283`, and passed on inputs differing by one JSON file. The ROADMAP exit rule is explicit: a green run after a red one on unchanged input closes nothing. Likely mechanism — NOT verified, US-2 must confirm or refute it: `android/build.gradle.kts` (~line 85) passes `room.schemaLocation = $projectDir/schemas` to kapt; `android/schemas` is not in git; `:android:assemble` runs `kaptDebugKotlin` and `kaptReleaseKotlin` concurrently (run 34556064209 starts them at 02:51:02.2888 and 02:51:02.2893); both export `dev.amphora.store.UploadDatabase/1.json` into the one directory, and one can deserialize a file the other has created but not yet written. Room's documentation says the schema directory must be declared to Gradle as a task input/output and that exported schemas belong in version control; the Room Gradle Plugin (`androidx.room`, since Room 2.6.0, configures javac, KAPT and KSP) exists to do both.

**What this tasklist cannot do on its own: close Phase 1.** Closing needs a run on `main`, and chief merges locally without pushing. US-3 states exactly what the operator must do.

userStories.title: BackgroundSessionManager gets a concurrency model, and both ios compile errors go away because of it — not because a diagnostic was silenced
acceptanceCriteria: Before touching code, record the before-state in notes: the two error lines from `gh run view 34556064209 --log-failed`, verbatim, and the diagnostic list of a CLEAN local `swift build --package-path ios --scratch-path <fresh tmp dir> -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors -Xswiftc -strict-concurrency=complete`. The fresh `--scratch-path` matters: an incremental build prints no diagnostics for files it does not recompile, which reads as clean.

`BackgroundSessionManager` carries a written concurrency model on the type: every stored property, whether it is mutable, and which threads or queues touch it (the session's delegate queue, `DispatchQueue.main` in `urlSessionDidFinishEvents`, arbitrary callers of `setSystemCompletionHandler`). Every mutable property is made immutable or guarded by a lock available at the CURRENT minimums — iOS 15 / macOS 14, so `NSLock` or equivalent, not `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` (iOS 16+). Only then is `Sendable` declared on the class; `@unchecked Sendable` is acceptable if and only if the doc comment justifies each stored property. Declaring `Sendable` over an unguarded `var` is the defect restated, not the fix.

`NetworkGovernor.start()` no longer references a captured `var` inside the `Task` (the `[weak self]` capture is that var). The actor -> `NWPathMonitor` -> `pathUpdateHandler` -> actor edge stays weak: the monitor is owned by the actor, so a strong capture there is a retain cycle that `stop()` does not break. State in notes how the new code keeps it weak.

No dependency on ADR-0002: `git diff` shows `ios/Package.swift`'s `platforms:` unchanged, `TUSKitTransport.swift` still present and still returned by `TransportSelector.select` below iOS 17, and no `@available` / `#available` bump introduced to dodge a diagnostic.

None of these silencers appear in the diff: removing or weakening `-warnings-as-errors`; `@preconcurrency import`; `nonisolated(unsafe)`; `-strict-concurrency=minimal`; a `swiftLanguageVersions` / `swiftSettings` change; a `#if compiler(...)` guard around the affected code. Each turns the job green without answering who owns the concurrency model.

`BackgroundUploadStarter` (in `NativeResumableTransport.swift`) is reconciled with the new model — either kept with its doc comment corrected (it is no longer the only `Sendable` claim, and 'the Sendable redesign `BackgroundSessionManager` still needs' stops being true) or removed. Either way the line `        return TransferHandle(taskIdentifier: taskId, stagedRemainderPath: nil)` in `NativeResumableTransport.swift` stays byte-identical: it is the anchor of the `swift / I6` control in `Tests/Conformance/drift-control.sh`, and a missing anchor fails that script.

`.chief/verify.sh` builds Swift with the flag CI uses (`-Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`), closing the first bullet of docs/reference/continuous-integration.md § Known divergence as far as flags can; `.chief/tests/verify-skip-policy.sh` still passes. The `ios` CI job gains a first step printing `swift --version` and `xcodebuild -version`, so the next divergence names the compiler that produced it — run 34556064209's log does not.

After the fix, re-run the same clean complete-checking build and record its diagnostic list. `BackgroundSessionManager.swift:29` must be gone. `SQLiteUploadStore.swift:42:28` (`sqlite3_close(database)` in a nonisolated `deinit`) is a separate pre-existing finding: fix it or record it as out of scope with its exact text; it counts neither for nor against this story. Do not add `-strict-concurrency=complete` to CI unless the build is clean under it.

GATES: `swift build --package-path ios -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` exit 0; `swift run --package-path ios AmphoraPathTests` exit 0 printing `46 passed`; `Tests/Conformance/drift-control.sh --port swift` ending `2 control(s) ran, 0 skipped, 0 failure(s)`; `.chief/tests/verify-skip-policy.sh` exit 0; `.chief/verify.sh` exit 0 with its `Gradle build — no JDK on PATH` skip named as NOT green (CLAUDE.md §3). A local build cannot prove the CI errors are gone — CI's compiler is not this one, as measured above. That proof belongs to US-3.

userStories.title: The Room schema race is fixed where it starts: the plugin owns the directory, and the exported schema is committed
acceptanceCriteria: Establish the mechanism before fixing it: confirm or refute, from evidence rather than plausibility, that `Empty schema file` comes from the two variant kapt tasks sharing one `room.schemaLocation`. Record: the concurrent start timestamps of `:android:kaptDebugKotlin` and `:android:kaptReleaseKotlin` in a run log, the schema path each writes, and what `Database.exportSchema` does with a pre-existing schema file in Room 2.6.1 (from the published Room sources or release notes — cite the URL). If refuted, name the real mechanism and fix THAT. Do not ship the plugin swap as a fix for a cause that was never established.

The schema directory is configured by the Room Gradle Plugin: `id("androidx.room")` at the SAME version as `room-runtime` / `room-compiler` (2.6.1), declared `apply false` in the root `build.gradle.kts` and applied in `android/build.gradle.kts`, with `room { schemaDirectory("$projectDir/schemas") }`. The `kapt { arguments { arg("room.schemaLocation", ...) } }` block is removed — two mechanisms writing one directory is the race again. The comment explaining why `exportSchema = true` is deliberate moves with it. No KSP migration here: kapt's `Falling back to 1.9` warning is real and out of scope, because that swap is a `replace` tasklist, not a fix.

The exported schema for `UploadDatabase` version 1 (`UploadJob.SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`) is committed under `android/schemas/` at the path the plugin writes, and its bytes are Room's, not hand-written. There is no JDK on this machine, so obtain the file from CI: add a step to the `android` job, after `:android:assemble`, that fails when the generated schema differs from the committed one (for example `git status --porcelain -- android/schemas` non-empty => print the diff or the file, then exit 1). That step is both how the file is retrieved on the first push and the gate that stops a later entity change shipping without its schema. Room's docs say exported schemas belong in version control.

The `android` job log of the proving run contains zero lines matching `room.schemaLocation` — run 34556064209 has one: `warning: The following options were not recognized by any processor: '[room.schemaLocation, kapt.kotlin.generated]'` on `:android:kaptDebugUnitTestKotlin` — and zero `Schema export directory` warnings. Record both counts. `kapt.kotlin.generated` is kapt's own option and may survive in a residual warning; if it does, quote the line and say so rather than calling the warnings gone.

Do not read a green `android` job as evidence of this fix. The failure was nondeterministic and the job is green today without any change. The evidence is the established mechanism plus the configuration that removes it — the ROADMAP's 'fixed at the root (schema export configuration)'.

GATES: in the `android` job of a pushed `chief/140-ci-green-at-the-root` CI run — `./gradlew --no-daemon --stacktrace :android:assemble` SUCCESS, `./gradlew --no-daemon :android:testDebugUnitTest` SUCCESS with `ConformanceVectorsTest` PASSED, and the new schema-drift step SUCCESS — quoted with the run id. Locally, `.chief/verify.sh` exit 0 with `Gradle build` SKIPPED (no JDK), recorded as unverified here, not green.

userStories.title: One run id, every job green — and the record says exactly what still stands between this and Phase 1 closed
acceptanceCriteria: Push the branch (`git push origin chief/140-ci-green-at-the-root`; `ci.yml` builds `chief/**` on push) and quote the run id with every job's conclusion from `gh run view <id> --json jobs --jq '.jobs[] | "\(.name) \(.conclusion)"'`. All five jobs — `ios`, `android`, `conformance-fixture`, `verify-policy`, `react-native` — are `success`.

The `ios` job is observed REACHING and passing its later steps, not merely compiling: quote from that run's log the `Run Swift path tests` summary (`Amphora path tests: 46 passed ...`) and the `Swift drift negative control` summary (`2 control(s) ran, 0 skipped, 0 failure(s)`). Neither has ever executed in CI; their first execution is the deliverable.

Re-run that run on the same head sha (`gh run rerun <id>`) and quote the second attempt's job conclusions. Two consecutive green attempts on identical input is the minimum this repository accepts from a gate that has flipped its verdict on identical input before. One is not enough.

State Phase 1's exit condition in notes, verbatim from ROADMAP.md: 'one run id shows every job green, the `ios` job is observed reaching and passing its `swift run` and drift-control steps, and the Room kapt failure is either fixed at the root (schema export configuration) or reproduced on demand — a green run after a red one on unchanged input closes nothing.' Then list what the OPERATOR must do after the merge, because chief merges locally and makes no network call: (a) `git push origin main`; (b) `gh run list --branch main --limit 1`, then read that run — every job `success`, and `ios` reaching and passing `swift run` and the drift control; (c) `gh run rerun <id>` once and see it green again on the same sha; (d) only then mark the ROADMAP §1 'The CI gate is total' row and the Phase 1 section closed, citing both attempts.

Update the record with what was observed and nothing more. ROADMAP.md's Phase 1 table and its §1 'The CI gate is total' row, and docs/reference/continuous-integration.md § Known divergence (the single home of the Swift error count, now zero), each cite the branch run id and both attempts. This tasklist does NOT mark Phase 1 closed — the `main` run has not happened. Answer the ROADMAP §4 open question 'Who owns `BackgroundSessionManager`'s concurrency model?' by pointing at the model US-1 wrote. Revise CLAUDE.md §3 'Corollary: CI's Swift is stricter than yours' so it no longer says the job is red today, and keep its warning that the two toolchains differ. Add a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry. Wherever a doc's claim changed, add a dated `## Corrections` entry (CLAUDE.md §6).

GATES: `.chief/verify.sh` exit 0 (with `Gradle build` SKIPPED named, not green); `Tests/Conformance/check-single-fixture.sh` exit 0; the two CI attempts above, each quoted by run id and attempt number with all five job conclusions.
